_meta.purpose: D-148: what https://insidelabel.ai/.well-known/assetlinks.json says (api/main.py builds the standard Digital Asset Links statement from this). Chrome opens the Play app (package ai.insidelabel.app.f, D-149) without an address bar only when the SHA-256 of the certificate that signed the installed build is listed here.
rules: Two fingerprints, both kept: the upload key (Sushil's, from keytool on his laptop) and Google's app signing key (Play Console, Test and release > App integrity, after the first upload; D-012). An install from Play is signed with Google's key, so the address bar only goes once that one is here.
Each sha256 is 32 pairs of upper-case hex digits joined by colons, exactly as keytool and Play Console print it. tests/test_assetlinks.py fails on any other shape.
An empty list, a missing file or a malformed one serves a 404: no statement rather than a wrong one.
Fingerprints are public (anyone can read them from the served file); the keys and their passwords are never in this repo.
